text: Writing clean code is an important skill for every programmer. Clean code is easy to read and understand, even for someone who did not write it. One key idea is using clear naming conventions. Variables and functions should have names that explain what they do, like `calculateTotal` instead of `calc`. Another important point is keeping functions small and focused on one task. This makes the code simpler to test and fix. Clean code is also easier to maintain over time. When you need to update or add features, readable code saves you hours of confusion. In short, writing clean code helps you and your team work faster and make fewer mistakes.
